reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor found four errors in my round-1 set that all pushed value down: $50/W capex (company-implied ~$38/W; Bernstein $36.5-39.5B/GW), a flat 0.90/yr age curve (Uvik per-watt evidence ~0.82; my own read of the Uvik/Ornn index values gives 0.77-0.86), Cursor acquisition SBC expensed while its shares were in the count, and Musk's 1,302M Mars/100-TW restricted shares counted as economic. I verified each at source (424B4 text, Ex.99.1, cnyes, Uvik, Q2/Q3 call transcripts) and applied them, added the $8B cash Grain 800 MHz spectrum deal (new, WSJ via Broadband Breakfast; Ex.99.1 H1-27 close), costed Starlink and Space SBC, and moved P/E to the ex-TSLA median 18x. Capacity: 2.2 GW at end-October and 200-220k GB300/month give ~8.3 GW at YE27 plus Rubin uplift -> 8.8 GW (not 13; management's own norm is ~25% project slippage). Price: hold ~$50/W-yr through 2027 (CFO above $30-50, renewals higher, indices up 15-20% in October), fade 42/33/27/23 to ~$21 by 2033 vs a ~$19.9 break-even; 2028 collapse 28%, hold into 2029 22%. Engine: 12x EV/EBITDA $131.89, SOTP $53.76, 18x P/E $91.32 -> $92.52 fair value (Kilian's 15x/27x: $115.61). The 12-month price is not my fair value: the 2027 ramp is visible and the fade is a 2028+ story, so the base ($126) keeps a premium; bear $75 is convergence on an early repricing, bull $235 is 13 GW with pricing into 2029.
